primary_scope: All 22 pre-existing rankings at 3 capacities plus dense, crossed 2 ranking sources x 2 detector outputs; each output keeps its prior dense-Thun threshold
sensitivity_scope: EMA current/absolute at all 3 capacities plus dense, crossed 2x2 at each of the two already frozen numeric dense thresholds; no new threshold selection
decomposition: Shared-dense identity cohort fixed within each sequence/regime. Let y[d,r] be kept shared instances for output d and ranking r. Ranking contribution = ((y01-y00)+(y11-y10))/2; output-path contribution = ((y10-y00)+(y11-y01))/2. Sum equals diagonal change exactly in integer half-counts. Also report both order-specific effects and interaction. Output-locked output-path includes threshold differences; common-numeric regimes remove that difference.
full_outcomes: Own-dense preservation, shared-dense preservation, all eligible GT recall, TP/lost/gained/FP, small-object subset, trajectory-equal preservation, sampled loss runs with censoring, and mask overlaps
interpretation_forks: If ranking effects persist on a fixed output and at common numeric thresholds, output confidence changes alone cannot explain them
If output-path effects dominate under fixed ranking, do not attribute the diagonal decline solely to the residual criterion
If signs or interactions differ across recordings, report the heterogeneity rather than a universal explanation
limits: Descriptive software intervention using cached full-network candidates; no new GPU inference, training, calibration or deployable policy
All five recordings already exposed to development; same architecture, two checkpoints, one adaptation-order seed
Interlaken has only two dense-detectable trajectories; query counts are not independent sample counts
Shared cohort is diagnostic, never a replacement for full GT and own-dense outcomes
Equal output-position capacity is not equal total compute or matched evaluation false positives
No environmental causal claim, risk/importance correction, physical skip, energy result or formal H1/H2/H3 verdict
